en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga,
Chapter on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on Exhortation 30.
The Training Rule on Sitting Together in Secret.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the former wife of the Venerable Udāyī had gone forth among the bhikkhunīs.
She used to come frequently into the presence of the Venerable Udāyī, and the Venerable Udāyī also used to go frequently into the presence of that bhikkhunī.
On one occasion, the Venerable Udāyī sat down in private with that bhikkhunī, alone with her.
Those monks who were of few desires... they complained, grumbled, and spread it about:
"How can the Venerable Udāyī arrange to sit alone with a bhikkhunī in private?"... [The Buddha asked:
"Is it true, Udāyī, that you arranged to sit alone with a bhikkhunī in private?"
“It is true, Blessed One. The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him:

“… How can you, foolish man, arrange to sit alone with a bhikkhunī in private? This is not for the benefit of non-believers, nor for the increase of the faithful; it causes those without faith to lose their faith and makes the faithful waver. It is not fitting for a recluse, does not lead to the goal of the holy life, and I say it does not conduce to revulsion, dispassion, cessation, peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, or nibbāna. And how, foolish man, could you even think of doing such a thing?”
“Monk, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:
‘If any monk should sit down in private, one-on-one, with a nun, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But whoever" means whoever such a person...
"a monk" means... [as before].
... pe ... this is the meaning intended here by "bhikkhu.
A "bhikkhunī" is one who has received full ordination in both Saṅghas.
"Saddhim" means together;
"eko ekāya" means one with one.
He is both a bhikkhu and a bhikkhunī.
"In secret" means in the privacy of the eye or in the privacy of the ear.
Regarding the eye, what is called "secrecy" cannot be seen when the eye is being rubbed, or when the eyebrows are being raised, or when the head is being lifted.
Regarding the ear, what is called "secrecy"...
It is not possible to hear ordinary conversation.
"Should sit down" means:
if a monk sits down or lies down close to a nun who is sitting, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If a bhikkhunī sits down either close to or near a seated bhikkhu, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Or, if both are seated or both are lying down, there is an offense of expiation.
If one is alone with another and, perceiving it to be a secluded place, one engages in sitting together with that person, there is an offense of expiation.
If one who is in private, being doubtful, sits alone with a woman, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one who is in private, perceiving it as such, sits alone with a woman, there is an offense of expiation.
If one who is not in private, perceiving it as such, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one who is worthy is suspected of being so, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one who is worthy perceives them as worthy, there is no offense.
There is no offense—
Whoever has a wise companion stands and does not sit down,
looking toward arahantship.
If he sits down while distracted,
it is no offense for one who is insane or for an original offender.
The tenth training rule concerning the preparation for a journey is finished.
This concludes the third chapter on Exhortation.
Here is its summary verse:
May the Unconquered One who has passed away accept this gift of food;
may he ferry me across the journey like a boat, and may I enjoy [its fruit].
One [gives] ten to one.
